finding.claim: iconUrl is stored without any validation and fetched server-side by the nightly sync job, so an authenticated user who can call PUT /profile can make the server issue GET requests to arbitrary URLs (internal hosts, loopback, cloud metadata 169.254.169.254, file-adjacent schemes supported by URI/HttpClient are limited to http/https). Response bytes are fetched (ofByteArray) and could be exposed if the icon is later served or cached.

trace.note: this.iconUrl = icon stored with no scheme/host/IP validation (only webhook is validated at line 12)
sync() builds request from URI.create(iconUrl) and sends GET; no allowlist, no private-IP blocking, no DNS pinning

finding.guards_checked: The regex check at line 12 only covers webhook, not icon. No scheme allowlist, host allowlist, or private/loopback/link-local blocking on iconUrl. Non-reachability considered: update() is annotated as PUT /profile and sync is a nightly job that reads the stored field, so entry point is reachable. Webhook (line 21) was ruled out: matches() is a full-string match against a fixed host https://hooks.example.com/ + 20 alphanumerics, and java.net.http.HttpClient does not follow redirects by default (Redirect.NEVER) unless the injected client is configured otherwise, so it is not reported.

verdict.reason: src/Profile.java:16 stores the request-controlled `icon` with no validation (the regex at line 12 covers only `webhook`), and src/Profile.java:23 sends a GET to URI.create(iconUrl) with no scheme/host/IP restriction; no other file references Profile or iconUrl.
